name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default.

This ensures keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one click, solving the most common blocker for screen-reader and keyboard-only users. The trade-off is a small permanent UI element, but it’s worth it—users with disabilities gain immediate access, while others rarely notice it.

name: Reader
text: A large, high-contrast skip link risks pushing primary content below the fold on small screens, hurting mobile users. A better alternative is a hidden skip link triggered by keyboard focus, but it must be clearly visible when focused to avoid confusing first-time users. The argument settles with user testing: measure task completion for keyboard-only users on mobile and desktop before and after changes.
